title: Adaptive token-pocketing + probe-eviction for paged-attention KV reuse
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our paged-attention KV cache shows poor reuse for workloads with bursty long-tail sequences (chat sessions with intermittent long prompts). Current slab allocation and LRU-driven eviction cause high fragmentation and repeated cold prefill during decode, increasing tail latency and GPU cycles.

Goal: Implement an adaptive 'token-pocketing' layer that groups recent contiguous token spans into compact pockets (lightweight metadata structures) and a probe-based eviction mechanism that evaluates pocket reuse probability before evicting pages. Tight integration with kernel-selection heuristics should allow avoiding unnecessary kernel handoffs on prefill and favor compact execution paths for high-probability pockets.

Scope: design, prototype, perf benchmarks on hosted workloads, migration plan for existing running allocators, compatibility tests with dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype reduces re-prefill GPU token count by >= 18% on long-tail chat traces compared to baseline (measured on n1-standard cluster)
Tail decode P95 latency improvement >= 12% on sample ingress with 99th percentile sequence lengths > 2k tokens
No regression (>2%) in median latency for short-sequence workloads
Kernel-selection integration chooses compact decode kernels for >= 85% of pocket-prefill cases in the experiment
Feature gated rollout path with config flags and telemetry; unit + integration tests merged; migration doc and rollback plan authored
implementation_notes: Design pocket metadata as a compact 48-bit descriptor per pocket: (start_token_idx, length_bucket, last_touch_ts, reuse_score_quantile). Keep descriptor footprint < 8 bytes/page to limit overhead.

Pocketing runs eagerly on prefill completion and lazily during background GC passes to amortize CPU work. Probe-based eviction samples candidate pages and computes a lightweight reuse_score using exponential decay on last_touch and cross-tenant affinity heuristics.

Kernel hints: expose a pocket-id in the prefill descriptor so the kernel selector can prefer microfusion-friendly kernels (short-seq optimized) when pocket length < 256 and affinity score > threshold.

Tradeoffs: pocketing increases allocator metadata and background CPU cycles; we tune probe frequency and sampling window to keep overhead < 1% of serving CPU budget. If overhead rises, fallback to pure LRU path.
Compatibility: provide a migration toggle (runtime flag) to enable pocketing per-tenant. For Dedicated/Private, require explicit opt-in and document KMS/audit implications (no user data in metadata).
Bench harness: extend perf-driver to replay anonymized chat traces with token timestamps; add microbench for kernel-selection decision path when pocket metadata present.
risk_assessment: Medium: incorrect reuse heuristics could increase unnecessary retention, starving other tenants and hurting aggregate throughput
Mitigations: rate-limited global pocket reservations and backpressure on prefill when memory pressure high; implement a decay policy that reduces pocket priority under contention
Operational: need new observability (pocket reuse rate, probe eviction counts) to detect regressions quickly
